content.title: Memoised or cached function: every argument that affects the result must be in the cache key (cached authorization decisions key on user + resource + action)
content.problem: A shared-kit memo helper keys on the first argument by default. A custom key covering only user and site omitted the action, so a cached decision for one action was returned for another. Results depended on request order: a contractor refused costs, then denied the work order view, or a view allowed then costs allowed. Users saw 403/404 or wrongly granted access depending on what they requested first.
symptoms: Same request returns 200 or 403 depending on which request came earlier
Cached permission check returns the answer for a different action or permission
Access works after a refresh/cache expiry but not on the first call after another endpoint
Directory/slow-dependency call count lower than the number of distinct decisions
content.component: caching / memoisation wrapper around an authorization check

environment.cache: shared-kit memo with custom key function and TTL

steps: Run the access cache tests, which interleave requests varying only the later arguments (action), and count calls to the slow directory lookup

rootCause.explanation: The memo key function returned a string from user and site only, ignoring the action argument, which determines the permitted roles. Distinct decisions collided on one cache entry, so the first decision computed for a (user, site) was reused for every action. The shared kit's default is also first-argument-only, which invites this mistake.

failedAttempts.approach: Trust the tests that exercised one action per user
failedAttempts.whyFailed: Order dependence only shows when calls vary just the later arguments and interleave

failedAttempts.approach: Explain the user reports as a per-site denial
failedAttempts.whyFailed: The report was explained by a refused costs request cached before the view on the user's own site, not by a site denial; the initial test also had a wrong expectation for a supervisor assigned to two sites

solution.description: Give the memo an explicit key containing all result-affecting arguments, normalised: JSON.stringify([user, Number(siteId), action]). JSON array avoids separator collisions; Number() makes string and number ids share an entry. Keep the cache and TTL; no vendor edits.
solution.tradeoffs: Cache is still unbounded and a TTL delays revocation of access changes; the number of entries grows with distinct user/site/action combinations.

appliesWhen: Adding or reviewing a cache, memo or key function for a function with several arguments
A result depends on request order or on what was called earlier
Using a library memo whose default key is the first argument only
notApplicableWhen: The function takes a single argument that fully determines the result
The failure is a stale value after the underlying data changed (TTL or invalidation issue) rather than a key collision

reviews.notes: Accurate and generic; backed by fail ev-mv035yms-0168a842 and pass ev-mv03a9s1-011232ec, and my reruns ev-mv03b4xg-018c0dcd, ev-mv03b9d3-0176d0ba. Source matches the described key.
